servinfosub.title: Step 1: Customer Complaint Analysis
servinfosub.ptxt: Record details of problem (failure, complaint) and how it occurred as described by the customer. For this purpose, such a questionnaire form shown below will facilitate collecting information required for proper analysis and diagnosis.

servinfosub.title: Step 2: DTC Check
servinfosub.ptxt: Check DTC stored in BCM memory.

topic.title: In case that current DTC is detected:
topic.ptxt: Perform applicable DTC troubleshooting for current DTC and repair or replace faulty parts.

topic.title: In case that history DTC is detected:

s1.ptxt: Record DTC and then clear DTC once.

Referring to “Circuit Diagram” and “Trouble Area” in applicable DTC troubleshooting, check related parts that are prone to cause intermittent trouble (e.g. wire harness, connector, etc.) for detected history DTC.

attention3.ptxt: Do not follow DTC troubleshooting flow for intermittent trouble.

topic.title: In case that there is no DTC:

s1.ptxt: If there is “Symptom Diagnosis” procedure for any possible cause, perform corresponding “Symptom Diagnosis” procedure.

servinfosub.title: Step 3: Trouble Symptom Confirmation
servinfosub.ptxt: Check if what customer claimed in “Customer Questionnaire” is actually found in vehicle and if that symptom is found (This step should be shared with customer if possible.). Also, check if DTC is detected or not.

servinfosub.title: Step 4: Final Confirmation Test
servinfosub.ptxt: Check that the problem symptom has gone and keyless start system is free from any abnormal conditions. If what has been repaired is related to malfunction DTC, recheck DTC and check that no DTC is indicated. If history DTC is detected, clear DTC.
